correctness.rationale: For every |a|>=2, Cassini-type quadratic identity proves each gcd divides N=a^4-1. Strong divisibility gives d|F_{n-1} iff z(d)|n-1. The Fibonacci companion matrix gives Q^{z(d)}=u_d I (mod d), u_d^2=(-1)^{z(d)} (mod d), and hence a unique residue class modulo L_d=z(d)ord(u_d) for each eligible local divisor predicate, with exact sharp period. Euler totient divisor recovery proves P(a) is a period and the preservation of all local predicates proves it divides every possible period. Finite Möbius inversion gives the density formula and positivity spectrum. This reasoning covers n=1, d=1 and either sign of a, excluding |a|<=1 as stated. Embedded stdlib verifier checks every signed 2<=|a|<=12 shift through a full candidate period, all strict subperiod divisors, all local events and exact fractional frequencies; finite tests are not relied upon for generality.

originality.rationale: Rahn–Kreh (2018) explicitly leave the all-integer-shift smallest-period question as Problem 13. The source already includes scalar residue powers, but not the sharp local occurrence periods or their global least-common-multiple minimality proof. The 2020/2022 general recurrence theorems produce sufficient periods while acknowledging that smallest periods may differ; the 2025 case-by-case ±4 results do not imply the all-shift theorem. Actual indexed literature searches on least periods, ranks, exact gcd distributions and equivalent formulations found no matching result; residual primary-source/full-text and unindexed-literature risks are listed, not treated as proofs of uniqueness.

value.rationale: The exact least period for arbitrary equal integer shifts is an explicit named Problem 13 in Rahn–Kreh 2018; this settles it uniformly with a finite arithmetic formula using at most order-four units. The same local structure gives exact natural density of every gcd value and a complete computable value spectrum, natural finer invariants that boundedness and sufficient periods cannot supply. This is a whole infinite natural family, not a numerical table or parameter relabeling; no asymptotic claim or complexity guarantee is needed.
